html:
Ġgantija is a pair of megalithic temples on the island of Gozo, built about 3600 BCE. They are among the oldest free-standing stone buildings in the world, older than Stonehenge and the pyramids of Egypt.

Farmers whose ancestors had come from Sicily raised them from huge blocks of limestone, some weighing many tonnes. Later Gozitans thought only giants could have built them, hence the name. Inside are curved rooms with altars, and the temple builders also carved figures of very fat human bodies.

The temple culture of Malta lasted over a thousand years and left more than thirty temples, among them Ħaġar Qim and Tarxien, and the underground Hypogeum. It ended about 2500 BCE for reasons still unknown. The temples are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and part of the wider world of megalith builders.
